study_identification.author_journal_year: Yu et al., Human Brain Mapping, 2024
study_identification.title: Behavioral and brain morphological changes before and after hemispherotomy

study_characteristics.study_objective: To quantify gray matter volume (GMV) changes before and after hemispherotomy in pediatric refractory epilepsy, relate GMV changes to behavioral recovery, and assess whether preoperative GMV features predict postoperative behavioral scores.

dataset_name.answer: Multi-site aggregated dataset (ABIDE; BCP; Calgary Preschool MRI Dataset; Children School Functions and Brain Development Project; Chinese Color Nest Project; Healthy Brain Network; Human Connectome Project-Development; Infant Brain Imaging Study; Multicenter Database on Perinatal Factors in Child Brain-Mind Development; Pediatric Imaging, Neurocognition, and Genetics; Pixar). Supplementary Table S1 lists ABIDE I and II separately and adds CPMD and PeriCBD.
dataset_name.reason: Main text lists 11 MRI datasets; Supplementary Table S1 provides per-dataset details including ABIDE I/II, CPMD, PeriCBD, site counts, and scanner fields.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: LMEM for pre/post behavioral and voxelwise GMV changes (individual random effects; fixed effects include MRI-to-surgery interval and covariates); Pearson correlations between GMV change in significant clusters and behavioral change; predictive modeling of postoperative scores using preoperative GMV with nested LOOCV (SVR, LASSO, Ridge), significance via permutation; group comparison via Wilcoxon signed-rank on squared residuals.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Both groups showed widespread GMV increases in contralateral cerebrum and ipsilateral cerebellum and GMV decreases in contralateral cerebellum; contralateral cerebellar GMV decrease correlated with behavioral improvement in right but not left hemispherotomy; preoperative GMV predicted postoperative behavioral scores at the individual level.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: LMEM revealed significant postoperative increases in age-adjusted and raw GMV across the contralateral cerebrum (Left: t=6.92/7.21; Right: t=7.44/7.69; all p<.001) and ipsilateral cerebellum (Left: t=6.95/8.59; Right: t=8.53/9.16; all p<.001). Contralateral cerebellum showed decreased age-adjusted GMV (Left: t≈−8.32; Right: t≈−7.73; p<.001), with raw GMV decrease for Left (t≈−6.93, p<.001) and no change for Right (t≈−1.60, p=.11). Change in contralateral cerebellar GMV correlated with behavioral improvement in Right (r=−.64, p=.007) but not Left (r=−.10, p=.73). Preoperative GMV predicted postoperative behavioral scores significantly across SVR, LASSO, and Ridge; performance was better in Left vs Right by Wilcoxon tests (RR p=.002; SVR p=.007; LASSO p=.02).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Not explicitly stated. Potential considerations: no explicit harmonization or site/scanner modeling for multi-site normative training data; normative model performance metrics (e.g., EV/MSLL) not reported; single-modality (T1 GMV) focus; modest patient sample sizes; reliance on manual hemisphere masking and visual QC.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Constructed a symmetric pediatric T1 template; applied voxelwise GPR via PCNtoolkit to obtain age/sex-adjusted GMV Z-scores; used nested LOOCV for individual-level postoperative behavioral prediction from preoperative GMV features.

general_notes.general_notes: Supplementary Table S1 enumerates datasets (ABIDE I/II, BCP, CPMD, CBD, CCNP, HBN, HCPD, IBIS, PeriCBD, PING, Pixar) with site counts and scanner field strengths. Patient MRI acquired on a Philips Achieva 3T at a single center.
